channel.title: The Daily Digest
channel.description: One top story from each of my chosen publications, updated daily.

item.title: NYT: Election Officials Fear Trump Administration’s Interference in Midterms Voting
item.description: State and local plans for Election Day include how to react to potential ICE raids, misbehavior by federal election monitors and attempts to seize votes or machines.

item.title: NPR: Bolsonaro's Party accepts Brazil election defeat, but he refuses to concede
item.description: Brazil's opposition party accepts Lula's election victory, but Flávio Bolsonaro won't concede, while President Trump calls the vote "rigged" without offering evidence.

item.title: BBC News: Minimum wage set to rise but 18-20 year-olds will not get bigger increase
item.description: Chancellor John Healey will reveal the new pay rates in the Budget, and has also announced measures to help households with the cost of living.

item.title: The Guardian: Elon Musk’s AI Odyssey review – the dullest, most pointless riposte possible to Christopher Nolan’s brilliant epic
item.description: It is hardly a shock that Grok AI’s interpretation of Homer is as meaningless as a laptop screensaver. The only surprise would be if Musk accepted defeat graciously. Which he won’t Think back. Do you remember when Elon M…

item.title: Al Jazeera: Israel election turnout highest in 50 years as voting continues
item.description: Almost 45 percent of Israeli voters had cast their ballots by mid-afternoon.

item.title: Ars Technica: Apple iPhone Duo review: Two screens, two experiences, two thousand dollars
item.description: I respect Apple's first crack at a foldable phone, but I'm not sure I like it.

item.title: WIRED Backchannel: UK Politician Jess Asato Got Deepfaked. Now She’s Taking xAI to Court
item.description: Jess Asato’s public campaigning for victims of online abuse put her in the crosshairs of Grok’s deepfake scandal. Then the UK member of parliament became a victim of the abuse herself.

item.title: WIRED Science: NASA’s Oldest Martian Spacecraft Have Been Running for Decades. Here’s How
item.description: Two orbiters have long outlasted their expected lifespans and completely reshaped our understanding of the Red Planet, all while operating 140 million miles from Earth.

item.title: WIRED Business: AI Agents Are Media’s New Favorite Audience
item.description: As agents go mainstream, some publishers are hoping that people will pay for content tailor-made for AI—not humans.

item.title: The New Yorker: Can Democrats Win Back Labor?
item.description: Two years ago, Sherrod Brown, who built his career as an avatar of blue-collar frustration, lost his Senate seat in Ohio as working-class voters defected to Trump. Now he and his party are looking to make up lost ground.

item.title: New York Mag The Cut: Will Jay-Z Give Us a Beyoncé Super Bowl Cameo or What?
item.description: The upside of choosing yourself to perform at halftime is you get to invite your wife.

item.title: New York Mag Curbed: Chinatown Residents Sue to Stop Manhattan Jail’s Late-Night Construction
item.description: A Manhattan judge issued a surprisingly quick ruling that temporarily halts work after 6 p.m.
